title: Be Careful What You Wish For
subtitle: 許願要小心：雅各布斯〈猴爪〉
source: 原創導讀；小說原文依 Project Gutenberg《The Lady of the Barge》所收〈The Monkey's Paw〉（1902，公版），背景依 Wikipedia〈The Monkey's Paw〉，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: W. W. Jacobs, “The Monkey's Paw”, in The Lady of the Barge (1902), Project Gutenberg

beginner.title: Three Wishes
paras: Mr and Mrs White and their son Herbert live in a small house in England. One night, an old soldier friend, Sergeant-Major Morris, visits them. He shows them a strange thing: a dried monkey’s paw. He says an old holy man in India put a spell on it.
懷特夫婦和他們的兒子赫伯特住在英格蘭的一棟小房子裡。一天晚上，一位當過兵的老朋友——莫里斯士官長——來拜訪他們。他給他們看一樣奇怪的東西：一隻乾枯的猴爪。他說，印度一位年老的聖人在上面施了咒語。

The paw can give three people three wishes each. But the holy man wanted to show that fate controls our lives, and people who try to change it will be sorry. Morris throws the paw into the fire. Mr White quickly takes it out and keeps it.
這隻猴爪能讓三個人各許三個願望。但那位聖人想證明命運主宰我們的人生，試圖改變命運的人會後悔。莫里斯把猴爪丟進火裡。懷特先生立刻把它拿出來，留了下來。

Later, Herbert jokes that his father should wish for two hundred pounds to pay for the house. Mr White makes the wish. Nothing happens. Herbert laughs and says the money might drop on his head from the sky. But the next day, a man comes from the factory where Herbert works. Herbert has died in an accident with a machine.
後來，赫伯特開玩笑說，父親應該許願要兩百英鎊來付房子的錢。懷特先生許了願，什麼事也沒發生。赫伯特笑著說，錢說不定會從天上掉到他頭上。但第二天，赫伯特工作的工廠來了一個人：赫伯特在一場機器意外中過世了。

The company says it is not responsible, but it gives the family some money: exactly two hundred pounds. The wish came true, but in the worst possible way. Mrs White is full of grief. About ten days later, she makes her husband wish for their son to be alive again.
公司說他們不負責任，但給了這家人一筆錢：剛好兩百英鎊。願望實現了，卻是以最糟糕的方式。懷特太太悲痛欲絕。大約十天後，她逼丈夫許願讓兒子復活。

That night, someone knocks loudly at the door. Mrs White runs to open it. But Mr White remembers how terrible the accident was. He finds the paw and makes his third and last wish. The knocking stops. When the door opens, the road is empty. This 1902 story asks: should we try to control fate?
那天晚上，有人用力敲門。懷特太太衝去開門。但懷特先生記得那場意外有多可怕。他找到猴爪，許下了第三個也是最後一個願望。敲門聲停了。門打開時，路上空無一人。這個 1902 年的故事問我們：我們該試著掌控命運嗎？

intermediate.title: Be Careful What You Wish For
paras: W. W. Jacobs’s “The Monkey’s Paw”, first published in Harper’s Monthly in September 1902, begins on a cosy, stormy evening. Mr and Mrs White and their grown son Herbert are visited by Sergeant-Major Morris, a family friend who served with the British Army in India. As the evening goes on, he produces a small, dried-up object: a mummified monkey’s paw.
W．W．雅各布斯的〈猴爪〉，1902 年 9 月首次刊登於《哈潑月刊》，故事開始於一個溫馨卻風雨交加的夜晚。懷特夫婦和他們已成年的兒子赫伯特，迎來了莫里斯士官長的拜訪——一位曾在印度隨英軍服役的家族朋友。隨著夜深，他拿出一個小小的、乾癟的東西：一隻木乃伊化的猴爪。

According to Morris, an old holy man put a spell on it to show “that fate ruled people’s lives, and that those who interfered with it did so to their sorrow.” Three men may each have three wishes. Morris admits he has had his, and says the first owner’s third wish was for death. He throws the paw into the fire, but Mr White rescues it. “If you must wish,” Morris warns, “wish for something sensible.”
根據莫里斯的說法，一位年老的聖人在猴爪上施了咒語，要證明「命運主宰人的一生，而干涉命運的人必將後悔」。三個人可以各許三個願望。莫里斯承認他已經許過了，還說第一位主人的第三個願望是求死。他把猴爪丟進火裡，懷特先生卻把它救了出來。「如果你非許願不可，」莫里斯警告，「就許個合理的願望。」

At Herbert’s joking suggestion, Mr White wishes for two hundred pounds to finish paying for the house. Nothing seems to happen. Herbert even jokes that the money might drop on his head from the sky. The next day, a stranger arrives from Maw and Meggins, the company where Herbert works. Herbert has been “caught in the machinery”. The company admits no responsibility but offers compensation for his services: two hundred pounds. Morris had said that the paw’s wishes come true so naturally that people might call it coincidence.
在赫伯特開玩笑的提議下，懷特先生許願要兩百英鎊，好付清房子的錢。似乎什麼都沒發生。赫伯特甚至開玩笑說，錢說不定會從天上掉到他頭上。第二天，一個陌生人從赫伯特工作的「茂與梅金斯公司」來訪：赫伯特「被捲進了機器裡」。公司不承認有任何責任，但為了他的服務提供補償金：兩百英鎊。莫里斯曾說，猴爪的願望實現得太自然，人們可能會說那只是巧合。

Overcome with grief, Mrs White insists that her husband use the second wish to bring Herbert back. He hesitates, remembering that their son has been dead for ten days and could be recognised only by his clothing. Still, he wishes: “I wish my son alive again.” Late that night, a loud knocking begins at the front door.
悲痛欲絕的懷特太太，堅持要丈夫用第二個願望讓赫伯特回來。他猶豫了，因為他記得兒子已經死了十天，而且只能靠衣服才認得出來。但他還是許了願：「我希望我的兒子復活。」那天深夜，前門響起了猛烈的敲門聲。

As Mrs White struggles to unlock the door, her husband searches desperately for the paw and makes his third and final wish. The knocking stops. When the door opens, the street is empty. Jacobs never tells us exactly what was outside, or what the last wish was. The story leaves readers with a chilling lesson: wishes that try to cheat fate may bring results far worse than the problems they were meant to solve.
就在懷特太太拚命要打開門鎖時，丈夫慌亂地找到猴爪，許下了第三個、也是最後一個願望。敲門聲停了。門打開時，街上空無一人。雅各布斯從未明說門外到底是什麼，也沒說最後一個願望是什麼。這個故事留給讀者一個令人不寒而慄的教訓：試圖欺騙命運的願望，帶來的結果可能遠比原本想解決的問題更糟。

advanced.title: Fate, Chance and the Horror of Getting What You Want
paras: “The Monkey’s Paw”, by the English writer W. W. Jacobs, first appeared in Harper’s Monthly in September 1902 and was reprinted later that year in his collection The Lady of the Barge. Its premise is as old as folklore — three wishes granted by a magical object — yet Jacobs transforms it into one of the most influential horror stories in English. It was adapted for the stage as early as 1903 and first filmed in 1915, and its title has become shorthand for any wish that comes true in a terrible way.
英國作家 W．W．雅各布斯的〈猴爪〉，1902 年 9 月首次刊登於《哈潑月刊》，同年稍後收錄於他的小說集《駁船上的女子》。它的設定和民間故事一樣古老——一件魔法物品實現三個願望——但雅各布斯把它變成了英語世界最具影響力的恐怖故事之一。它早在 1903 年就被改編成舞台劇，1915 年首次被拍成電影，而它的標題也成了一種簡稱，用來形容任何以可怕方式實現的願望。

The story’s horror depends on restraint. The White family’s evening is domestic and affectionate; the visitor, Sergeant-Major Morris, entertains them with stories of India. When he produces the mummified paw, he explains that a holy man placed a spell on it “to show that fate ruled people’s lives, and that those who interfered with it did so to their sorrow.” His own experience is conveyed through silences and a whitening face rather than description. When he throws the paw into the fire and Mr White retrieves it, Morris offers a final, ominous instruction: “If you must wish, wish for something sensible.”
這個故事的恐怖建立在節制之上。懷特一家的夜晚溫馨而充滿親情；訪客莫里斯士官長用印度的故事逗他們開心。當他拿出那隻木乃伊化的猴爪時，他解釋，一位聖人在上面施咒，「要證明命運主宰人的一生，而干涉命運的人必將後悔」。他自己的經歷，是透過沉默和發白的臉色，而不是描述來傳達的。他把猴爪丟進火裡、懷特先生又把它撿回來時，莫里斯留下了最後一句不祥的叮嚀：「如果你非許願不可，就許個合理的願望。」

The first wish is modest and almost comic: two hundred pounds to clear the debt on the house, suggested by the light-hearted Herbert. Morris had warned that the paw’s effects happen so naturally that one might attribute them to coincidence, and that is precisely the horror that follows. A representative of Maw and Meggins arrives to report that Herbert has been “caught in the machinery”; the firm “disclaim all responsibility” but, in consideration of his services, offers compensation of exactly two hundred pounds. The wish is granted with grotesque literalness, and no supernatural event need be seen at all.
第一個願望謙卑得近乎滑稽：在輕鬆愛笑的赫伯特提議下，要兩百英鎊來還清房子的債。莫里斯曾警告，猴爪的效應發生得如此自然，人們可能會把它歸因於巧合——而接下來的恐怖正是如此。茂與梅金斯公司的代表前來通報，赫伯特「被捲進了機器裡」；公司「不承擔任何責任」，但考量到他的服務，提供了剛好兩百英鎊的補償金。願望以一種怪誕的字面方式實現了，完全不需要讓人看到任何超自然事件。

Grief then drives the second wish. Mrs White demands that her husband wish Herbert alive, dismissing his reminder that their son has been dead ten days and could be identified only by his clothing. “Do you think I fear the child I have nursed?” she cries. Mr White obeys, and in the dark the knocking begins — first faint, then a “perfect fusillade of knocks reverberated through the house.” While his wife struggles with the bolt, he finds the paw and “frantically breathed his third and last wish.” The knocking ceases, and the door opens on an empty road.
接著，悲傷驅使了第二個願望。懷特太太要求丈夫許願讓赫伯特復活，完全不理會他提醒兒子已經死了十天、只能靠衣服辨認。「你以為我會怕我親手帶大的孩子嗎？」她喊道。懷特先生照做了，黑暗中敲門聲響起——先是微弱的，接著「一陣密集如槍林彈雨的敲門聲在屋內迴盪」。就在妻子奮力拉開門閂時，他找到猴爪，「慌亂地低聲許下了第三個、也是最後一個願望」。敲門聲停止，門打開，外面是一條空蕩蕩的路。

Jacobs never states what stood outside or what the final wish was, and this withholding is the source of the story’s enduring power: readers supply the horror themselves. Beneath the supernatural surface lies a serious idea. Each wish attempts to override the ordinary course of events — poverty, death, grief — and each produces a cost greater than the problem it addressed. Whether one reads the paw as magic or the events as cruel coincidence, the story leaves an uncomfortable question about the limits of human control and the wisdom of accepting what cannot be changed.

雅各布斯從未說明門外站著的是什麼，也沒有說最後一個願望是什麼，而這種留白正是這個故事歷久不衰的力量來源：讀者會自己補上恐怖。在超自然的表面之下，藏著一個嚴肅的想法：每一個願望都試圖凌駕事情的正常發展——貧窮、死亡、悲傷——而每一個都帶來比它所要解決的問題更大的代價。不論你把猴爪讀成魔法，還是把這些事件讀成殘酷的巧合，這個故事都留下了一個令人不安的問題：關於人類掌控的極限，以及接受無法改變之事的智慧。

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How the Whites paid for their small house.
How a holy man made a paw from a monkey.
Why soldiers often travel to faraway India.
A magic paw whose wishes come true in terrible ways.
beginner.evidence: The wish came true, but in the worst possible way.
beginner.why: 全文：猴掌讓願望成真，代價卻很可怕。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：付房貸是第一個願望的目的。
以偏概全：聖人下咒只是猴掌的來歷。
以偏概全：印度只是猴掌的來歷。

beginner.q: What does “it” in “Mr White quickly takes it out and keeps it” refer to?
options: The fire.
The monkey’s paw.
The house.
The money.
beginner.evidence: Morris throws the paw into the fire.
beginner.why: 前一句：Morris 把猴掌丟進火裡。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：火是猴掌被丟進去的地方。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：房子是他們住的地方，不是被撿回來的。
時序錯置：錢是後來的事。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Herbert died in a car accident.
Morris made the first wish in the White family’s home.
The company gave the family exactly two hundred pounds.
Mrs White made the third wish.
beginner.evidence: it gives the family some money: exactly two hundred pounds
traps: 張冠李戴：是被機器捲入。
張冠李戴：許願的是 Mr White。
張冠李戴：第三個願望是 Mr White 許的。

beginner.q: What did Mr White most likely wish for the third time?
options: That whatever was at the door would go away.
That he could have two hundred more pounds.
That Herbert would knock on the door louder.
That Sergeant-Major Morris would come back.
beginner.evidence: The knocking stops. When the door opens, the road is empty.
beginner.why: 許完第三個願望，敲門聲停了，門外空無一人。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：兩百英鎊是第一個願望。
正反顛倒：敲門聲停止了。
捏造：Morris 沒再出現。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Wishes that try to cheat fate may bring worse results.
The Whites became rich and happy through the paw.
Morris sold the paw to the family for two hundred pounds.
Herbert’s death was clearly caused by magic.
intermediate.evidence: wishes that try to cheat fate may bring results far worse than the problems they were meant to solve
traps: 正反顛倒：他們失去了兒子。
捏造：他把猴掌丟進火裡。
正反顛倒：作者說可能被當成巧合。

intermediate.q: What does “compensation” in the third paragraph mean?
options: A machine used in a factory.
A reward for winning a prize.
Money paid to make up for a loss.
A spell placed on an object.
intermediate.evidence: offers compensation for his services: two hundred pounds
intermediate.why: 公司不承認責任，但為他的服務給付一筆錢以彌補損失。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：機器是事故原因。
一字多義：compensation 不是比賽獎金。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：咒語是猴掌的來歷。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Morris still had all three of his wishes.

The story was first published in 1920.
Herbert worked for the British Army.
intermediate.evidence: says the first owner’s third wish was for death
traps: 正反顛倒：他已經用過了。
數字錯位：1902 年。
張冠李戴：在軍隊服役的是 Morris。

intermediate.q: Why does Mr White hesitate before the second wish?
options: Morris had told him never to make a wish.
He wanted to wish for more money instead.
He had already lost the monkey’s paw.

intermediate.evidence: remembering that their son has been dead for ten days and could be recognised only by his clothing
traps: 正反顛倒：Morris 說要許就許合理的願。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：錢是第一個願望。
正反顛倒：他還拿著猴掌。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To prove that the holy man’s spell was real.
To show how the story builds horror through restraint.
To describe the life of soldiers in India.
To explain how the Whites paid off their house.
advanced.evidence: The story’s horror depends on restraint.
advanced.why: 第二段起分析：克制的寫法讓讀者自己補上恐怖。
traps: 過度推論：作者說可以當魔法，也可以當巧合。
以偏概全：印度只是背景。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：付房貸是第一個願望的目的。

advanced.q: What does “grotesque literalness” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: A long letter sent by the company.
A funny story told by the family at dinner.
A machine at the factory making loud noises.
A wish coming true exactly, but horribly.
advanced.evidence: The wish is granted with grotesque literalness
advanced.why: 願望「一字不差」地實現（剛好兩百英鎊），方式卻很恐怖。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：公司是派人來，不是寫信。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：第一個願望本來有點好笑，但不是這個詞的意思。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：機器是事故原因。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The story was first filmed in 1915.
The firm accepted full responsibility for Herbert’s death.
Morris described his own wishes in great detail.
The story was first published in The Lady of the Barge.
traps: 正反顛倒：公司不承認責任。
正反顛倒：他用沉默和臉色表達。
時序錯置：先刊在 Harper’s Monthly。

advanced.q: Why does the author say “readers supply the horror themselves”?
options: Readers are asked to write their own ending.
The story includes many frightening pictures.
Jacobs never says what was outside or what was wished.
Morris explains every event in great detail.
advanced.evidence: Jacobs never states what stood outside or what the final wish was
traps: 張冠李戴：直接請讀者決定的是〈美女還是老虎〉。
捏造：故事沒有插圖，恐怖來自留白。
正反顛倒：他幾乎什麼都沒說。

reflections: If you had three wishes but every wish might come true in an unexpected way, what would you wish for — and how would you word it carefully?
Is the story really about magic, or could everything be explained by coincidence? Use evidence from the article to support your view.

The story’s horror depends on restraint. The White family’s evening is warm and affectionate, and their visitor, Sergeant-Major Morris (an old soldier friend), entertains them with stories of India. When he produces a dried monkey’s paw, he explains that a holy man placed a spell on it “to show that fate ruled people’s lives, and that those who interfered with it did so to their sorrow.” Morris throws the paw into the fire, but Mr White pulls it out. “If you must wish,” Morris warns, “wish for something sensible.”
故事的恐怖建立在克制上。懷特一家的夜晚溫馨又親密，來訪的老軍人朋友莫里斯士官長向他們說著印度的故事。當他拿出一隻乾枯的猴爪時，他說一位聖人對它下了咒，「為了證明命運支配人的一生，凡是干涉命運的人，都會因此悲傷」。莫里斯把猴爪丟進火裡，懷特先生卻把它拿了出來。莫里斯警告：「如果你非許願不可，就許個合理的願望。」

The first wish is modest and almost comic: two hundred pounds to clear the debt on the house, suggested by the cheerful son, Herbert. Nothing seems to happen. The next day, however, a man from Maw and Meggins arrives to report that Herbert has been “caught in the machinery”. The firm, which admits no responsibility, offers compensation of exactly two hundred pounds. So naturally does the wish come true that no supernatural event need be seen at all.
第一個願望很小，幾乎有點好笑：要兩百英鎊來付清房子的債，是開朗的兒子赫伯特提議的。似乎什麼都沒發生。然而第二天，茂與梅金斯公司派人來，說赫伯特「被捲進了機器裡」。公司不承認任何責任，但提供了剛好兩百英鎊的補償金。這個願望實現得如此自然，根本不需要看到任何超自然現象。

Grief then drives the second wish. Mrs White demands that her husband wish Herbert alive, brushing aside his reminder that their son has been dead for ten days and could be recognised only by his clothing. Mr White obeys, and in the dark a knocking begins, faint at first and then louder. While his wife struggles with the lock, he finds the paw and makes his third and last wish. The knocking stops, and the door opens on an empty road.
接著，悲痛驅使了第二個願望。懷特太太要丈夫許願讓赫伯特復活，完全不理會丈夫提醒：兒子已經死了十天，只能靠衣服辨認。懷特先生照做了，黑暗中開始響起敲門聲，起初很輕，後來越來越響。妻子還在和門鎖奮戰時，他找到猴爪，許下第三個、也是最後一個願望。敲門聲停了，門打開時，外面只有空蕩蕩的路。

Jacobs never states what stood outside or what the final wish was. It is this silence that gives the story its lasting power, because readers supply the horror themselves. Beneath the magic lies a serious idea. Each wish tries to override the ordinary course of events — poverty, death, grief — and each produces a cost greater than the problem it addressed. Whether we read the paw as magic or the events as cruel coincidence, the story leaves an uncomfortable question about the limits of human control.
雅各布斯從沒說門外站著什麼，也沒說最後一個願望是什麼。正是這份沉默，讓這個故事歷久不衰，因為讀者會自己補上恐怖。在魔法之下，藏著一個嚴肅的想法：每個願望都想推翻事情的正常走向——貧窮、死亡、悲傷——而每個願望都帶來比原本問題更大的代價。不論把猴爪看成魔法，還是把一切看成殘酷的巧合，這個故事都留下一個令人不安的問題：人能掌控的範圍究竟有多大？

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why the White family moved to a new house.
How to find a magic monkey’s paw in India.
How a horror story uses restraint to explore the cost of controlling fate.
How W. W. Jacobs became a famous film director.
questions.evidence: It is this silence that gives the story its lasting power
questions.why: 全文：故事如何靠克制製造恐怖，以及干涉命運的代價。
traps: 捏造：他們是想付清房貸，沒有搬家。
以偏概全：印度只是猴爪的來歷。
張冠李戴：他是作家，故事後來被拍成電影。

questions.q: What does “restraint” in the second paragraph mean as used in the passage?
options: Holding back details instead of showing everything.
Tying someone up so they cannot move.
Spending very little money on a house.
Refusing to listen to stories about India.
questions.evidence: Jacobs never states what stood outside or what the final wish was.
questions.why: 克制：不把一切寫明，讓讀者自己補上恐怖。
traps: 字面誤讀：restraint 也有束縛的意思，但這裡指寫作上的克制。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：房貸是第一個願望。
捏造：一家人很愛聽故事。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Mrs White made the third wish.
Morris made the first wish in the Whites’ home.
Herbert had been dead for two days.
The firm offered exactly two hundred pounds.
questions.evidence: offers compensation of exactly two hundred pounds
traps: 張冠李戴：第三個願望是懷特先生許的。
張冠李戴：許願的是懷特先生。
數字錯位：原文說已經死了十天。

questions.q: Why does the author say the story’s horror “depends on restraint”?
options: Because the family is calm and never afraid.
Because the most frightening events are left unseen.
Because Morris refuses to tell any stories.
Because the story is very short.
questions.why: 作者手法：最可怕的部分都沒寫出來，由讀者自己想像。
traps: 正反顛倒：一家人最後非常恐懼。
正反顛倒：莫里斯說了很多印度的故事。
以偏概全：篇幅不是恐怖的來源。
